REPLAYED 2026-09-03: THE FIRST HALF HOLDS AND THE SECOND HALF IS FALSE. The line reads "Selection: Cherry" and the log line reads "Set selection to Cherry from code.", so the button ran and the state changed; all five row bands of the plain List still measure exactly (255, 255, 255), i.e. nothing at all was painted. A tap paints and a programmatic selection does not: tapping row 3 of the neighbouring split-view List (pixel 480, 1338) tints a text-free strip of that row to (237, 237, 237) while its four neighbours stay at 255, and 237 is exactly the 0x32a1a1a1 list selector composited over white (255*0.804 + 161*0.196 = 236.6). The responsible line is Sources/AndroidBackend/AndroidBackend+List.swift:146, listView.setItemChecked(Int32(index), true), reached from Sources/SwiftCrossUI/Views/List.swift:269. setItemChecked records the choice in AbsListView mCheckStates and, for a row that is not android.widget.Checkable, expresses it only as View.setActivated on rebind -- and these rows are plain custom containers built by CustomListAdapter.setViews with no activated state in their background, so the flag is stored and never drawn. It is the same trap as the comment three lines above it, which rejects setSelection because it is "accepted and draws nothing"; the replacement is accepted and draws nothing either, one level further in. NOT FIXED HERE -- reported for a decision. SECOND RECORDING 2026-09-04: BOTH HALVES NOW HOLD. The Cherry row band measures 237 -- the ListView's own selector colour 0x32a1a1a1 over white, the same value a tapped row gave -- across y 1284-1374, and the label reads "Selection: Cherry". The cause was in the drawing, not the binding: `AbsListView` calls `setActivated(true)` on a checked row whose view is not `Checkable`, and these views are plain containers with no drawable that answers `state_activated`, so the flag arrived and nothing painted it. Fixed by giving each row a foreground StateListDrawable; foreground rather than background, so a row's own `.background()` is not taken over by selection
